content:
PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL
Machine Learning Engineer
Osijek, Croatia | petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606 | github.com/pzn-ml-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Machine Learning Engineer with 5+ years of experience in natural language processing (NLP), document classification, and developing machine learning solutions from research and prototyping through production deployment. Experienced in fine-tuning transformer models, production model serving and monitoring, and MLOps practices using MLflow and Azure. Current doctoral research focuses on processing the Croatian language.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Machine Learning Engineer | Slavonica Document AI d.o.o. | Osijek
03/2023–Present
- Developed an automated classification model for incoming documents—including invoices, contracts, and administrative decisions—for public-sector clients, achieving 94% accuracy across 23 classes.
- Fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R transformer models for named entity recognition in Croatian documents.
- Introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry; deployed models as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and Azure App Service.
- Established production model-quality monitoring for data drift, with weekly reporting.
- Mentor two students during their professional internships.

Data Scientist | Baranjska kreditna banka d.d. | Zagreb (remote from Osijek)
09/2021–02/2023
- Developed customer-churn prediction models using gradient boosting and LightGBM for the sales team.
- Analysed customer complaints and classified topics using TF-IDF with logistic regression, later using fastText.
- Created SQL reports using an Oracle data warehouse.

Research Project Assistant | Faculty of Applied Informatics, Drava University
10/2020–08/2021
- Built a corpus of Croatian legal texts and annotated the data.
- Wrote Python scripts to support the research work.

EDUCATION
Doctoral Studies in Computer Science | Drava University | In progress, since 2022
Research topic: Named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts

MSc in Computer Science (Mag. ing. comp.) | Drava University | 2020

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy, pandas, NumPy, SQL, MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Git, Linux

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native) | English (C1) | German (B2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, professionally structured, and easy to scan. The experience bullets use relevant technical terminology and include a strong measurable result: 94% accuracy across 23 classes. The progression from research to data science and machine learning engineering is credible, and the doctoral research is relevant to NLP. The main content issue is that the summary appears to imply more than five years specifically as a Machine Learning Engineer, whereas the documented Machine Learning Engineer role began in March 2023. The CV also omits the relevant 2024 publication listed in the original candidate information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly: it uses standard section headings, chronological experience, conventional date formats, plain text contact details, and a readable technical-skills list. It contains strong keywords including Python, NLP, transformer models, model serving, monitoring, MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, and Azure App Service. AI screening probability is moderate to strong for general ML/NLP and production ML roles, but lower for this specific position because the CV does not show chat assistants, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), data versioning, orchestration beyond MLflow, feature engineering, or data ingestion pipelines. These are candidate-to-role gaps rather than formatting defects, so they should not be added without supporting evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV strongly matches the degree, Python, Azure, model serving, production monitoring, transformer fine-tuning, NLP, and MLflow requirements. It also demonstrates relevant customer- and text-oriented work through document classification and customer-complaint topic classification, which is directionally relevant to customer-support AI. However, the candidate's material does not show experience with chat assistants or RAG, feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, or explicit data versioning. The material also does not establish at least four years of experience specifically as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping systems to production: the documented ML Engineer role runs from March 2023 to the present, while earlier work is described as Data Scientist and Research Project Assistant. These are genuine alignment gaps, not CV defects. The CV does not provide evidence of CI/CD, automated tests, orchestration tools such as Airflow or Kubeflow, or integration with wider product engineering teams. The document does show ownership-related evidence through introducing MLflow and establishing production monitoring, and teamwork evidence through mentoring two students, but it does not need to force additional culture language unsupported by the candidate information.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Summary, change “Machine Learning Engineer with 5+ years of experience” to a precise formulation such as “Machine Learning Engineer with production experience in NLP, document classification, and machine learning solutions, backed by more than 5 years of combined research, data science, and machine learning experience.” This avoids implying that the candidate has held a Machine Learning Engineer role for more than five years, which is not supported by the documented employment dates.

MINOR — In the Education section, add the supported publication as a separate “PUBLICATIONS” section after Education or before Technical Skills: “Zlatarić-Novosel, P. et al. (2024). Named entity recognition for Croatian administrative documents. Workshop on Slavic Language Processing.” Keep the venue wording accurate to the original information and do not describe it as a peer-reviewed publication unless supported.

MINOR — In the Professional Experience section under “Machine Learning Engineer | Slavonica Document AI d.o.o.”, consider changing “Established production model-quality monitoring for data drift, with weekly reporting” to “Established production model-quality monitoring for data drift and produced weekly reports.” This is slightly more direct while preserving the documented evidence.

MINOR — In the Technical Skills section, retain “Azure ML” and “Azure App Service” as separate entries or write “Azure ML, Azure App Service” so both cloud-service keywords are parsed independently. Do not add AWS or GCP.
critique.critical_issues: Potential experience overstatement: “Machine Learning Engineer with 5+ years of experience” may be interpreted as five or more years specifically in a Machine Learning Engineer role, but the original candidate information documents that title only from March 2023 onward. Correct the summary wording to distinguish total relevant experience from time in the Machine Learning Engineer role. No unsupported tools or technologies such as RAG, chat assistants, AWS, GCP, Airflow, Kubeflow, or CI/CD were added, but they must not be introduced without evidence.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional CV with a clear Machine Learning Engineer headline, reverse-chronological experience, relevant education, publication, technical skills, and measurable outcomes. The 94% accuracy result and specific model, cloud, deployment, and monitoring details add credibility. The document is concise and easy to scan. Its main limitation is not general CV quality but role-specific evidence: it does not demonstrate customer-support assistants, RAG, feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, CI/CD, automated testing, or four full years specifically in an ML Engineer role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard, ATS-friendly section headings, plain text formatting, conventional dates, and a searchable technical-skills list. It includes strong matches for Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, NLP, model serving, monitoring, MLflow, Docker, Azure, FastAPI, and SQL. Estimated AI/ATS screening probability is medium-high for general Machine Learning Engineer roles and moderate for this particular vacancy because several must-have terms are absent: chat assistants, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), data versioning, feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, and four years as an ML Engineer. The document would benefit from using the exact phrase “model serving” in the experience bullets and grouping MLOps/cloud skills more explicitly, but it should not add unsupported technologies or experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with the degree, Python, Azure, MLOps/MLflow, model serving, model monitoring, transformer fine-tuning, text-data preparation, and production ML requirements. The Croatian NLP and document-classification background is relevant to customer-support automation, ticket routing, and language-model work. However, the candidate material does not show experience with chat assistants or RAG, and it does not establish four full years specifically as a Machine Learning Engineer: the ML Engineer role begins in 03/2023. Feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, and explicit data versioning are also not evidenced. These are genuine job-alignment gaps rather than CV-writing defects. Evidence of ownership and teamwork is present through introducing MLflow, establishing production monitoring, and mentoring two students, although the CV does not explicitly demonstrate CI/CD, automated testing, cross-functional product integration, or orchestration beyond MLflow.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ATS ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Machine Learning Engineer experience section under Slavonica Document AI, revise the deployment bullet to use the job description’s exact supported terminology. For example: “Implemented model serving by deploying models as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and Azure App Service; introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry.” This makes model serving, Azure, MLflow, and model registry explicit without adding unsupported experience.
2. In the Technical Skills section, reorganize the existing skills into searchable categories without adding new tools: “Programming: Python, SQL; Machine Learning/NLP: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy; Data: pandas, NumPy; MLOps and Deployment: MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Azure App Service; Tools: Git, Linux.” This improves keyword visibility and parsing.
3. In the Professional Summary, change “production model serving and monitoring” to “production model serving, model monitoring, and MLflow-based MLOps” so the summary mirrors the advertisement’s terminology while remaining fully supported by the existing experience.
4. In the Machine Learning Engineer experience section, make the monitoring result more explicit by changing “Established production model-quality monitoring for data drift and produced weekly reports” to “Established production model monitoring for data drift and produced weekly model-quality reports.”
